Let the four eigenvalues of the Hessian be
\[
\lambda\in\{1,3,5,7\}.
\]
After \(t\) steps, the \(\lambda\)-coordinate is multiplied by
\[
m_1(\lambda)=1-\alpha_0\lambda,\quad
m_2(\lambda)=(1-\alpha_0\lambda)(1-\alpha_1\lambda),
\]
\[
m_3(\lambda)=(1-\alpha_0\lambda)(1-\alpha_1\lambda)(1-\alpha_2\lambda).
\]
Since all update maps are diagonal in the same basis,
\[
R=\max_{\lambda\in\{1,3,5,7\}}
\max\left\{
\frac5{14}|m_1(\lambda)|,\frac57|m_2(\lambda)|,|m_3(\lambda)|
\right\}.
\]

We claim the minimum is \(3/10\), attained at
\[
(\alpha_0,\alpha_1,\alpha_2)=\left(\frac4{25},\frac12,\frac27\right).
\]

For this triple,
\[
1-\frac4{25}\lambda=\left\{\frac{21}{25},\frac{13}{25},\frac15,-\frac3{25}\right\},
\]
so the first-step weighted maximum is
\[
\frac5{14}\cdot \frac{21}{25}=\frac3{10}.
\]
After the second step,
\[
m_2(\lambda)=\left\{\frac{21}{50},-\frac{13}{50},-\frac3{10},\frac3{10}\right\},
\]
so
\[
\frac57\max |m_2(\lambda)|
=\frac57\cdot \frac{21}{50}
=\frac3{10}.
\]
After the third step, using \(\alpha_2=2/7\),
\[
m_3(\lambda)
=\left\{
\frac{21}{50}\cdot\frac57,
-\frac{13}{50}\cdot\frac17,
-\frac3{10}\cdot\left(-\frac37\right),
\frac3{10}\cdot(-1)
\right\},
\]
whose maximum absolute value is again \(3/10\). Hence \(R\le 3/10\).

Now prove no smaller value is possible. Suppose \(R\le 3/10\), and write
\[
u=\alpha_0,\qquad v=\alpha_1,\qquad w=\alpha_2.
\]
From the \(\lambda=1\) first-step constraint,
\[
\frac5{14}|1-u|\le \frac3{10}.
\]
Since \(0<u\le 1/2\), this gives
\[
u\ge \frac4{25}.
\]

If \(u=\frac4{25}\), then the \(\lambda=1\) second-step constraint gives
\[
\frac57\cdot \frac{21}{25}(1-v)\le \frac3{10},
\]
so \(v\ge 1/2\). Since \(v\le 1/2\), we get \(v=1/2\). Then the \(\lambda=1\) final-step constraint gives
\[
\frac{21}{50}(1-w)\le \frac3{10},
\]
so \(w\ge 2/7\). The \(\lambda=7\) final-step constraint gives
\[
\frac3{10}|1-7w|\le \frac3{10},
\]
so \(0\le w\le 2/7\). Thus \(w=2/7\).

It remains to rule out \(u>4/25\). The \(\lambda=1\) second-step constraint gives
\[
(1-u)(1-v)\le \frac{21}{50},
\]
so
\[
v\ge 1-\frac{21}{50(1-u)}.
\]
Also \(v\le 1/2\). Put
\[
P=(1-u)(1-v),\qquad Q=(7u-1)(7v-1).
\]
For \(u>4/25\), the above lower bound on \(v\) implies \(v>1/7\), so \(Q>0\).

The final-step constraints at \(\lambda=1\) and \(\lambda=7\) require
\[
P(1-w)\le \frac3{10},\qquad Q|1-7w|\le \frac3{10}.
\]
These intervals for \(w\) can intersect only if
\[
\frac7P+\frac1Q\ge 20. \tag{1}
\]
But on the interval
\[
1-\frac{21}{50(1-u)}\le v\le \frac12,
\]
the function
\[
h(v)=\frac7{(1-u)(1-v)}+\frac1{(7u-1)(7v-1)}
\]
is convex, so its maximum occurs at an endpoint. At the left endpoint, \(P=21/50\), and
\[
Q-\frac3{10}
=
\frac{21(u-\frac4{25})(\frac12-u)}{25(1-u)}>0,
\]
so \(h(v)<20\). At \(v=1/2\),
\[
h\left(\frac12\right)-20
=
\frac{4(175u^2-78u+8)}{(1-u)(35u-5)}<0
\]
for
\[
\frac4{25}<u\le \frac{46}{175}<\frac27.
\]
The upper bound \(u\le 46/175\) comes from the \(\lambda=7\) first-step constraint. Hence \(h(v)<20\), contradicting (1). Therefore \(u>4/25\) is impossible.

Thus the optimizer is unique and equals
\[
\alpha_*=\left(\frac4{25},\frac12,\frac27\right),
\]
with minimum value
\[
R_*=\frac3{10}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\left(\frac3{10},\left(\frac4{25},\frac12,\frac27\right)\right)}
\]
